rule_questions: Q1 relied-on model vs model-with-a-comparison: atomoxetine's filed pharmacology is an engagement model (ex vivo uptake, microdialysis) and no efficacy model was relied on; later members used the neonatal 6-OHDA juvenile rat (centanafadine 2012). Should the efficacy cell be empty, open with the 6-OHDA model in 2012, or carry the field-standard SHR that was only ever tested retrospectively? The brief's 'best model' rule points to 6-OHDA/untested; the drafter chose SHR because it alone has a published comparison.

Q2 inverse miss: `contra` says 'predicted wrongly', direction-agnostic, and ad-amyloid safety scores a missed harm, so a false negative can be contra in principle. But Dommett 2014 is a retrospective validation of a model nobody used for this class, its patient side is approval status (rule 5 tension), and the same SHR/5CSRTT setup also missed methylphenidate. Does a retrospective null in a non-relied-on model count as a wrong prediction by 'the model the class relied on'? I say no.

Q3 structural silence (#54): the drafter scored suicidality contra under '(or its silence)'. Animal models could not have been relied on: suicidal ideation has no animal readout, the 2005 boxed warning came from pooled paediatric trial meta-analysis (5/1,357 vs 0/851), and the antidepressant class warning of 2004 likewise had no preclinical basis. Ad-amyloid's contra is silence on an askable question (cognitive worsening is measurable in animals). Proposed test: silence is contra only if the harm was measurable in the model species at the time; otherwise the entry is dropped, not scored.

Q4 indeterminate dose test: Logan 2007 (human PET, published after Seneca 2006) found no dose effect and no plasma-occupancy relation, the opposite of the monkey's dose-dependent 38-82% / asymptotic prediction, but attributes it to signal-to-noise. The brief has no status for 'tested, could not resolve'; drafter kept untested. Agree, but the rule should say so.

Q5 engagement by juxtaposition: rule 1 requires a primary source that 'makes the comparison', yet cf-cftr scores Ramsey 2011 as same with no stated model comparison. Logan 2007 (comparison_stated=false, 24 male subjects of unstated health, direction only) is accepted here on that precedent; if the strict reading governs, both become untested.

Q6 label-dated entries: the brief dates by 'the year the comparison was published'. For a label-sourced comparison that means the first label version carrying the wording, which for Strattera 9.2 is unreadable (scanned 2002 PI); the drafter used approval year. Rule should say whether approval year is an acceptable proxy when the original label cannot be read. [Resolved for this entry: OCR of the 2002 printed label found the wording.]
